solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Beau with the chance to tour Quebec or pass on

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go all round it, so the shuffled letters surround the Quebec letter
letters left to chance fall into a random order, so Beau and the are shuffled

parts.note: Quebec is Q in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A dashing suitor gets the opportunity to travel round Quebec, or else lets it go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beau' looks like the subject of the sentence but is anagram fodder; 'chance' makes BEUEATH, which 'to tour' wraps round Q.
explanation.definitionFit: To bequeath is to hand property down by will, a formal way of passing something on.

clue.text: 'Bottomness.' What Ned in 'Deliverance' revealed for all to see where trousers originally dropped

indicators.note: dropped means that letter is let fall and another put in its place

parts.note: the actor Ned Beatty starred in the film Deliverance

indicators.note: originally asks for the first letter of trousers

parts.note: U is the film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for all

explanation.surface: Ned Beatty's infamous scene in Deliverance exposed his bottom when his trousers came down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' swaps the T (trousers originally) in BEATTY for U, the film rating for all audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: In particle physics the bottom quark is also called the beauty quark, and its quantum number bottomness is also called beauty.

clue.text: It could be an honour for hand or man on board

definitions.text: It could be an honour for hand
definitions.meaning: in bridge the ace, king, ..., jack and ten are honours held in a hand
a chess piece, a man on a chessboard

explanation.surface: An honour might go to a farmhand or to a man serving on a board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'honour' suggests a title awarded to a person; here it is a high card in a bridge hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The card is a bridge honour and the most powerful chessman.

clue.text: Former partner under extreme pressure say has to call up offering explanation

indicators.note: in a down answer, under means the next piece comes below the one before

parts.note: EP is the abbreviation for extreme pressure, as on lubricants
an ex is a former partner
eg, for example, is what say means here

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word is read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: to cite is to call, as a witness

explanation.surface: An ex-partner under great strain has to phone, wanting to explain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' sets EX below EP; 'up' turns CITE into ETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Epexegetic means adding words that explain what has gone before, so offering further explanation.

clue.text: Consulting a webpage is trendy: ingenuity's not required

indicators.note: not required means that part is dropped from the trendy phrase

parts.note: with it means fashionable, trendy
wit is ingenuity; the 's is ingenuity is

explanation.surface: Browsing a webpage is fashionable, and no cleverness is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit is a single visit to or request for a webpage.

clue.text: Passé as say Dolly Varden

definitions.meaning: out of date, no longer fashionable
a Dolly Varden is a wide flowered hat of the Victorian era, so an example of an aged piece of headgear

explanation.surface: Something is as out of fashion as a Dickens character.
explanation.walkthrough: Dolly Varden is a character in Dickens's Barnaby Rudge, and the broad, flower-trimmed hat named after her went out of fashion long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for anything stale or unfashionable, and literally describes a vintage bonnet.

clue.text: Luxembourg and its meandering border

parts.note: L is the international vehicle code for Luxembourg

indicators.note: meandering means winding about, so its letters wander

explanation.surface: Luxembourg and its winding frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A list is a border or edge, especially the selvage of cloth.

clue.text: Embarras de richesses for 100 European women likely to succeed?

indicators.note: embarras suggests a muddle, so the riches word is jumbled
for means one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A French phrase for having more riches than one can manage, applied to women who are bound to do well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' puts E in the place of C (100) in RICHESSES, and 'Embarras de' mixes the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Heiresses are women set to inherit, to succeed to an estate, with a pun on success.

clue.text: Flute playing goes over heads of all save those having aesthetic discernment

indicators.note: playing means fooling about, so the flute letters are rearranged
heads of asks for the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Flute music goes over the heads of everyone except those with refined taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' mixes FLUTE with A, S, T, the heads of all, save, those.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasteful means showing good taste, the faculty of aesthetic judgment.

clue.text: Perhaps Lincoln and Ely cut back white poplar

parts.note: Abe was the familiar name of Abraham Lincoln, the US president

indicators.note: back means the shortened city name is read in reverse
a word cut is docked of its final letter, here the cathedral city losing its tail

explanation.surface: Lincoln and Ely, two English cathedral cities, are cut back like a pruned tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln looks like the cathedral city beside Ely, but it is Abraham Lincoln. 'cut' takes the Y off ELY, and 'back' turns EL into LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Abele is the traditional name of the white poplar tree, Populus alba.

clue.text: Son also starts disturbances

parts.note: also means too
starts in the sense of jumps aside in alarm, as a horse shies

explanation.surface: A son also begins something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' looks like a verb of beginning but is the jumpy sense, as a startled horse shies.
explanation.definitionFit: Stooshie is a Scots word for a commotion, fuss or row.

clue.text: In outskirts of Cambridge packers may work here

indicators.note: letters that work are put to use in a fresh arrangement
outskirts are the edges of a place, the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: On the edge of Cambridge, workers who pack goods might be employed here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of' gives CE; 'may work' mixes it with IN and PACKERS. Cambridge Science Park lies on the city's northern edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A science park is a site for research businesses, the place the clue's 'here' points to.

clue.text: Hislop's rebuff?

parts.note: Ian Hislop edits the satirical magazine Private Eye, so a jibe from him is a slap printed in his magazine

explanation.surface: A snub delivered by Ian Hislop, the satirical editor.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means a snub or setback, and literally a mention in Private Eye, which Ian Hislop edits.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a humiliating rebuff, and the satirical magazine is commonly called the Eye.

clue.text: Spike's consuming passion fruit

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so the spikes hold the passion inside them

parts.note: spike's is read as spikes, tines being the spikes of a fork or antler
anger is a passion, a strong emotion

explanation.surface: Someone called Spike has a burning enthusiasm for passion fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passion fruit' reads as one item but splits: passion is ANGER, fruit is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangerines are small sweet citrus fruits, a kind of mandarin orange.

clue.text: Pool boundary in the country club

definitions.meaning: a lake or pond, as in Windermere
a dialect word for a boundary or landmark between fields
a Maori war club of greenstone or bone

explanation.surface: A swimming pool marks the edge of a country club.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: 'the country club' reads as one place but splits into 'in the country' and 'club', the Maori weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a lake, an old rural word for a border, and a Maori fighting club.

clue.text: Solve insider 4 or do 7 down?

indicators.note: solve in the sense of dissolve, loosening the letters into a new order

parts.note: 4 refers to the answer at 4 down, a webpage visit

explanation.surface: An instruction to crack the insider at 4, or to tackle 7 down.
explanation.walkthrough: To do 7 down means to do down the heiresses, depriving them of their inheritance.
explanation.definitionFit: To disinherit is to cut out of a will, doing would-be heiresses out of what they expected.

clue.text: Waiting times for delivery of 12, topped and, after pressing first, whisked and carbonated

indicators.note: whisked means beaten up together, so the letters are mixed
topped means having its top, the first letter, removed

parts.note: 12 refers to the answer at 12 across, the citrus fruits

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of pressing

parts.note: carbonated means given carbon, chemical symbol C

explanation.surface: A recipe: fruit is topped, pressed, whisked and made fizzy, all while waiting for a delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped' drops the T of TANGERINES; 'carbonated' adds C, and 'whisked' mixes ANGERINES with C into REGNANCIES, after P from 'pressing first'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pregnancies are the months of waiting before a baby is born, a birth being a delivery.

clue.text: Imperial eagle in Poland is poor man's weather glass

indicators.note: in means the imperial and eagle letters sit inside the Poland code

parts.note: PL is the international code for Poland
imp is an abbreviation for imperial
the erne is the sea eagle

explanation.surface: An imperial eagle living in Poland serves as a poor man's barometer.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarlet pimpernel closes its flowers in dull weather, earning the folk name poor man's weather glass.

clue.text: Social gathering for Maoris and others in the unit

indicators.note: others asks for every other letter in the phrase the unit, starting from the second

explanation.surface: A unit holds a social get-together for Maoris and other people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'others' means every other letter: tHe UnIt.
explanation.definitionFit: A hui is a Maori meeting or assembly, and in New Zealand any social gathering.

clue.text: Passover ritual minor prophet, not I, had set up

indicators.note: not I means the letter I is removed from the prophet's name

parts.note: Haggai is one of the twelve minor prophets of the Old Testament

indicators.note: in a down answer, set up means the word is written upwards, reversed

explanation.surface: A minor prophet, but not me, had established a Passover rite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not I' drops the I from HAGGAI; 'set up' turns HAD into DAH.
explanation.definitionFit: The Haggadah is the Jewish text read at the Passover Seder, setting out its ritual.

clue.text: Fish eye of Highlands Liberal

parts.note: ee is the Scots word for eye, used in the Highlands

explanation.surface: A fish catches the eye of a Liberal politician from the Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The eel is a long, snake-like fish.

clue.text: Mad hares in trips involving ego? They're among the ferns

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the self goes inside the jumble
trips in the sense of stumbles, so the letters fall into disorder

parts.note: the ego is the self, I

explanation.surface: Mad hares go on journeys, a question of their ego, and find themselves among the ferns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trips' jumbles MADHARESIN into MADENHAIRS and 'involving' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidenhair ferns are a delicate genus, Adiantum, so they belong among the ferns.

clue.text: Confrontational cardinal, a Spaniard, had one tortured

parts.note: HE, His Eminence, is the title of a cardinal
Don is a Spanish title for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A combative cardinal and a Spaniard had someone tortured.
explanation.walkthrough: A second wordplay leads to the same letters: 'tortured' rearranges HAD ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A head-on encounter is direct and confrontational, like a front-to-front collision.

clue.text: Government on alert in Edinburgh

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: The Scottish government is on alert in Edinburgh.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs, so on can be LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Gleg is a Scots word for quick-witted or alert, hence the Edinburgh tag.

clue.text: Not the Victoria station kelpie or was there ambiguity?

definitions.note: the kelpie is also an Australian sheepdog; this kelpie is not the one on a sheep station in Victoria

indicators.note: ambiguity suggests the letters can be taken in another order

explanation.surface: A question whether the kelpie at Victoria railway station was ambiguous.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria station suggests the London terminus, but Victoria is an Australian state and a station is a sheep farm, home of the kelpie sheepdog.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scottish folklore a kelpie is a shape-shifting water spirit that takes a horse's form.

clue.text: Just adjust

definitions.meaning: fair, correct, in accordance with justice
to set straight or correct, as to put a wrong in order

explanation.surface: A curt instruction simply to adjust.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: morally correct, and to restore to the proper position.

clue.text: Mitt, husband and author

explanation.surface: A list: mitt, husband and author.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple clue: 'author' is also a definition, since a hand can mean the person who made something, as in a work by another hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Mitt is slang for the human palm and fingers.

clue.text: I haven't the faintest idea about work master finished

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for finished goes round the work and master letters

parts.note: finished means done
a task is a piece of work
M is an abbreviation for master, as in MA

explanation.surface: Someone confesses ignorance about a work by a master that is now finished.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a colloquial way of saying one has no idea at all.

clue.text: Hamlet's 'piece of work' that's piece or work on board

definitions.meaning: Hamlet's speech asks what a piece of work is this creature, the human being
to crew or operate, as one does aboard a ship

explanation.surface: Hamlet's famous phrase about humanity, mixed up with chess pieces and work aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet says 'What a piece of work is a man'; the word also means a playing piece and, as a verb, to crew a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a human being, a chessman, and to staff a ship.

clue.text: Turnout in Oklahoma I had not articulated

parts.note: in American use a rig is a horse and carriage, a turnout
I had shortens to I'd

explanation.surface: A voter turnout in Oklahoma that someone failed to put into words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnout' suggests voters; here it is the American carriage-and-horses sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rigid has no joints to bend at, articulated meaning jointed.

clue.text: Had Lie group coordinated binary compound?

indicators.note: a group coordinated is arranged into order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Was a group called Had Lie organised around a two-part combination?
explanation.definitionFit: A halide is a binary chemical compound of a halogen with another element, such as sodium chloride.

clue.text: Antibiotic removes any nits over time

indicators.note: removes read as re-moves, moving the letters again

explanation.surface: An antibiotic gets rid of any lice eggs over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removes' reads as re-moves, signalling rearrangement of ANYNITS with T.
explanation.definitionFit: Nystatin is an antifungal antibiotic drug, used against yeast infections.
